title: Starter UX + Telemetry: Error Copy + Quickstart Cheatpack (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a compact starter "cheatpack" that combines: (A) first-60-seconds SDK quickstart flows, (B) recommended telemetry event contract for quick adoption, and (C) short, tested microcopy for error messages and onboarding hints. Target audience: internal SDK owners, docs writers, and the 3rd-party integrator doing a first integration in either mobile or serverless environments.

Goals (high level):
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-request to < 3 minutes for a polyglot developer.
- Provide a minimal event schema so product/infra can immediately onboard telemetry without back-and-forth.
- Ship consistent, low-friction error copy to prevent unnecessary support tickets.

Topline quickstart (60s flow):
1) Install (choose one):
   - npm: npm install @redwoodai/sdk --save
   - pip: pip install redwood-sdk
   - go: go get github.com/redwood-inference/sdk
2) Set API key (single env var): REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
3) Minimal snippet (JS):
   const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
   const r = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'Hello' });
   console.log(r.text);
4) Smoke validation (one-liners):
   - curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
   - python quick test: python -c "from redwood import Client; print(Client(api_key=\"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\").health())"

Notes to reader: short snippets above must be the default in any quickstart page. Avoid showing advanced config until after the first flow.

Telemetry contract (minimum viable):
- Event namespace: redwood.sdk.install, redwood.sdk.request, redwood.sdk.error, redwood.sdk.warmup
- Common fields (all events):
  - event_timestamp (iso8601), sdk_lang (js|py|go|java|swift), sdk_version, env (dev|staging|prod), integrator_id (optional), request_id (uuid)
- redwood.sdk.request payload: model, token_count_estimate, latency_ms, success (bool), route_hint (hosted|dedicated|private)
- redwood.sdk.error payload: error_code (enum), error_message (redwood copy), http_status, retryable (bool), stack_snippet (optional, sanitized)
- Sampling: default 1% for request events, 100% for error events, 10% for warmup.

Suggested event enums: error_code = [AUTH_INVALID, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, MODEL_NOT_FOUND, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, TIMEOUT, RUNTIME_ERROR]. Keep stable and documented.

Microcopy: short bits to include verbatim in SDKs and docs (tone: plain, helpful, actionable)
- Auth failure (401): "API key not found or invalid. Check REDWOOD_API_KEY and make sure it is active. If you recently rotated keys, restart your process."
- Quota exceeded (429): "You’ve hit your current plan’s request limit. Retry after a short delay or contact billing to request higher capacity."
- Timeout (504): "Request timed out — try again with a shorter prompt or enable streaming to reduce latency."
- Payload too large (413): "Input too large for this model. Try sending a shorter prompt or use chunking with the input-chunker utility."
- Model mismatch (404): "Requested model unavailable. Use 'redwood model list' or the Console to choose a compatible model."

Design notes on copy: include a 'next step' hint in every error message where feasible (e.g., a command to check key, or link to quota docs). Avoid jargon (no internal route names).

Integration quick heuristics (mobile vs serverless):
- Mobile (iOS/Android):
  - Never embed the primary API key in client builds. Ship an ephemeral proxy token flow in quickstart and show easiest reference: short-lived token mint endpoint + sample proxy code.
  - Recommend local caching (TTL 2s) to avoid tiny repeated requests from UI events.
- Serverless (AWS Lambda/GCP Functions):
  - Recommend connection reuse across invocations where possible (global client).
  - Highlight cold-start warmup: include redwood.sdk.warmup warmup event when a function initializes.

Smoke tests and gating:
- CI smoke: after install, run smoke script that: sets a test key, calls /v1/health, runs a generation with a 30-token prompt, asserts 200 and non-empty text.
- E2E gating for docs PR: include a tiny 'try-me' runner in the docs PR that executes in ephemeral environment (GH actions) with a read-only test key.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include a default client-side retry policy? (pros: fewer support tickets; cons: hides upstream rate limits)
- Decide canonical sampling rate for request events in enterprise orgs (suggest overrideable by org setting).
- Canonical command for rotating keys in place without downtime.
- Need final mapping of error_code enums to HTTP statuses (ask infra team).

Links & references:
- Confluence draft: DEVEXP-1420 (linked above)
- Existing SDK PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/328
- Related infra ticket: jira DX-789

Quick edit log (notes to self):
- 2024-10-08 Ava: initial outline and snippets
- 2024-11-02 Jonah: added telemetry contract and sampling suggestion
- 2025-01-15 Priya: tuned microcopy; added mobile/serverless heuristics

Publishing plan (next steps):
- Convert snippets into language-specific quickstart folders in the docs repo (assign: Miguel).
- Add telemetry event definitions to the events registry (assign: Jonah, infra).
- Run a small usability test with two partner integrators: time-to-first-success metric and copy comprehension survey (assign: Ava).

Unresolved: keep this as a draft until telemetry contract accepted and a single canonical smoke script is committed in the SDK repo.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally compact. The goal is a single page that any engineer can copy/paste into a README or a docs quickstart panel.
